html: The Iskonawa are a very small Panoan-speaking people of the Peruvian Amazon, from the upper Callería River in the Ucayali region of Peru. They avoided contact with outsiders until 1959, when missionaries brought a group of them out of the forest, and disease soon killed many. The survivors settled among the Shipibo, and their language now has only a handful of speakers. Some Iskonawa are believed to live still in isolation near the Brazilian border, and Peru has set aside a reserve for them, one of several for uncontacted peoples.
